blocks.text:
This journey brings together colonial cities, Inca archaeological sites, high-altitude roads and traditional Andean communities. In Peru, the route takes you through Lima, Cusco and the Sacred Valley before heading up to Lake Titicaca. After crossing into Bolivia via Copacabana, the journey concludes in La Paz.

## Trip highlights

Lima offers an introduction to Peru's colonial heritage and the vibrant life of its capital. In Cusco, the focus shifts to the history of the Incas: Sacsayhuamán, Q'enqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay are all located near the former capital of the Inca Empire.

One of the central days of the programme is dedicated to Machu Picchu. The journey to the ancient city passes through Aguas Calientes, followed by a bus ride up to the archaeological complex high in the mountains.

The Sacred Valley reveals another side of the Inca legacy. Chinchero preserves its weaving traditions, Moray is known for its concentric agricultural terraces, and Ollantaytambo was an important military, religious and agricultural centre.

The route then crosses the Andean Altiplano to Puno and Lake Titicaca. On the floating Uros Islands, houses and boats are built from totora reeds. The programme continues across the border into Bolivia through Copacabana and ends in La Paz.
